item: The preflight in airplane mode checks nothing, changes nothing and says so (source sweep, feed sweep, first-run job)
refs: PR #1570; R313 G1; found by PR #1558
summary: POST /api/sources/preflight in airplane mode used to record up to limit enabled sources as unreachable, overwrite each source's learned robots_allowed with None, append the verdicts to source_preflight.jsonl (the file has_run_before reads) and list the domains under unreachable. The feed preflight did the same with feed_preflight.jsonl. Now a refusal by the kill switch (our sentence at the start of the whole scrubbed text, R298) ends the sweep as complete false with skipped_offline (present only then) and a stopped sentence naming the kill switch; nothing is logged, no metadata is edited, the route rolls back, and the first-run job's pending stays true so the next online pass runs the preflight, and kick() now declines at the entry while the switch is engaged (Export's read of PR 1562 reproduced the defect independently). Every other failure, including a remote party's text that merely contains our sentence, stays unreachable. Answer to the boot question: a boot alone cannot stamp it (boot makes no pass and the job is kicked from the pass tail); before this change a manual POST while offline on a fresh install could, and so could Stop pressed between the scrape and the pass tail's kick. The consent ratchet's source-preflight GAP row became a named row proved by the real refusal. Mutants: the source changes stashed fail five of the seven original new tests; Export's two-source reproduction (both halves complete true, 12 feed records carrying the refusal, robots_allowed True to None) now ends incomplete with nothing logged and robots_allowed kept.
